name: Hyperimmunoglobulin D Syndrome

criteria.description: Recurrent febrile episodes (typically 3-7 days) starting before age 2
Elevated urinary mevalonic acid during attacks
GI symptoms (vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain) during attacks

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical picture of recurrent febrile episodes with elevated IgD and/or mevalonic aciduria, confirmed by MVK gene mutations. Eurofever criteria require genetic confirmation plus compatible features.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MKD is a spectrum: HIDS is milder, mevalonic aciduria (MA) is severe with neurological involvement. MVK enzyme activity: HIDS has 1-10% residual activity; MA has <1%.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent febrile episodes lasting 3-7 days with prominent cervical lymphadenopathy
pathognomonic.notes: Attacks often triggered by vaccinations, infections, or stress

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain with vomiting and diarrhea
Skin rash (maculopapular, urticarial, or erythema nodosum-like)

rare.notes: Much lower risk than FMF or TRAPS (~3%)

laboratory: Elevated serum IgD > 100 IU/mL (present in ~80%; not specific; IgD can be elevated in other autoinflammatory diseases)
Elevated urinary mevalonic acid during attacks
Elevated ESR, CRP, SAA during attacks
imaging: Abdominal imaging may show hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy during attacks
genetic: Most common mutation: V377I (associated with HIDS phenotype)
MVK enzyme activity 1-10% residual in HIDS; <1% in mevalonic aciduria
other: MVK enzyme activity assay in lymphocytes or fibroblasts
Mevalonic acid in urine (collected during attack)
Genetic testing is the gold standard for diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: FMF attacks are shorter (1-3 days) without prominent lymphadenopathy
TRAPS has periorbital edema and migratory myalgia
CAPS has urticarial rash, not maculopapular

redFlags: Neurological features (ataxia, developmental delay) suggesting severe mevalonic aciduria phenotype
references: van der Hilst JC, et al. Long-term follow-up, clinical features, and quality of life in a series of 103 patients with hyperimmunoglobulinemia D syndrome. Medicine (Baltimore). 2008;87(6):301-310.
Gattorno M, et al. Classification criteria for autoinflammatory recurrent fevers. Ann Rheum Dis. 2019;78(8):1025-1032.
Houten SM, et al. Biochemical and genetic aspects of mevalonate kinase and its deficiency. Biochim Biophys Acta. 2003;1637(3):190-200.
